title: Gaussian Scrooge Ensemble from Deep Thermalization in Free-Fermions
authors: Angelo Russotto, Katja Klobas, Pasquale Calabrese, Bruno Bertini
abstract: Deep thermalization indicates the emergence of universal ensembles of pure states in a subsystem after measuring its environment. We investigate this phenomenon in a free-fermion chain using local measurements that preserve Gaussianity and break particle-number conservation. Although the measurement outcomes provide partial information about local conserved charges within a finite subsystem, we argue that this information becomes negligible in the thermodynamic limit. This effective non-revelation underlies the emergence of a fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble, determined by the subsystem's generalized Gibbs ensemble. We construct this universal ensemble directly at the subsystem level and provide numerical evidence that it describes the late-time projected ensemble at finite temperature. Our results extend the description of thermalization in non-interacting integrable systems beyond the reduced density matrix to universal statistics of conditional pure states.
summary: This work explores deep thermalization in free-fermion systems by studying the ensemble of pure states remaining in a subsystem after measurements on its environment. The key finding is that in the thermodynamic limit, the statistics of these conditional states are universal, described by a fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble. This extends thermalization theory to account for the full statistics of quantum measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates deep thermalization, specifically how the universal ensemble of pure states in a subsystem emerges after local measurements on its environment.
main_result: The partial information about local conserved charges becomes negligible in the thermodynamic limit, leading to a universal description governed by a fermionic Gaussian Scrooge ensemble.
method: The authors analyze the projected ensemble by considering the first and higher moments of the conditional pure states resulting from projective measurements on the environment.
model_or_system: The system is a free-fermion chain governed by a Gaussian integrable Hamiltonian, bipartitioned into a subsystem A and an environment B.
key_observables: The projected ensemble, characterized by its correlation matrix and its moments, and the reduced density matrix $ho_A$.
important_parameters: The thermodynamic limit ($L_B 	o \infty$) and the late-time limit ($t 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system Hamiltonian is Gaussian and integrable, and that the partial information about conserved charges becomes irrelevant in the thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the process: an initial Gaussian state evolves, is measured on the bath B, and the resulting ensemble approaches a Gaussian Scrooge ensemble whose first moment matches the reduced GGE.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the measurement process, analyzing the role of local conserved charges, and deriving the universal form of the projected ensemble (the Scrooge ensemble) in the thermodynamic limit.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, non-equilibrium generalization of thermalization concepts, moving beyond just the reduced density matrix to characterize the statistics of conditional pure states, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems.
